rule: Orchestrators consult this policy for every dispatch. No silent deviation: any override requires a logged reason in the dispatch log. Edits to this file are owner-only.
runMachinesRule: Orchestrated runs may only launch on these hostnames. Workers run headless with permission prompts disabled, so the MACHINE is the sandbox, not the worktree: a worker can read anything the user can, including credentials in dotfiles. Dedicated or disposable machines only. Override per invocation with --unsafe-machine; the deviation is recorded in the run's event log and dispatch log.

build.notes: Load-balance across the Claude Max and Codex Max quotas. Neither vendor is default.

review.rule: Reviewer must be a different vendor than the author of the diff.
mandatoryWhen: diff touches auth, payments, data migrations, or deletion paths

research.notes: X search and research briefs. Output lands as a brief file in the project repo, consumed by build sessions.

subagent.rule: In-session delegation is routed by the shape of the work, not by how important it feels. Pick the cheapest tier that can carry the shape.
subagent.notes: The classes above route whole nodes of a run to a vendor. This section routes work a session hands to a subagent inside its own context, which is where most delegation actually happens.

haiku.notes: Deterministic edits with a known target. The instruction says exactly what to change, so the model is doing typing, not deciding.

sonnet.notes: Search-heavy and conclusion-light. The agent reads widely and reports what it found; the calling session draws the conclusion.

opus.notes: Work where the answer is a judgement rather than a list, including deciding whether the cheaper agents' findings are right.

breakEven.rule: Delegate when the reading-to-output ratio is high, or when the work splits across independent dimensions that can run at the same time.
breakEven.doNotDelegate: Work that is fast to do directly. Spawn overhead plus a cold context makes a one-line edit slower through a small model than done inline.
breakEven.notes: Written down here so it is decided once. The test is the ratio and the split, not the size of the file or the seniority of the task.

toolChoice.rule: Read-only work that produces findings goes to in-session subagents; work that produces committed diffs goes to `tars run`.
toolChoice.notes: Findings come back into the calling session's context and are cheap to discard. Diffs need a worktree, a critic and a merge, which is what the runner exists for.

resilience.rule: Capacity failures fail over without consuming a work retry. Cooldowns are circuit breakers, not sleeps inside provider processes.

evaluation.rule: Policy changes are proposed from dispatch-log evidence, never from orchestrator preference.
